condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: The query is a tryptamine derivative with a secondary aliphatic amine and a hydroxamic acid; its very low neutral fraction (0.01) and zwitterionic character predict poor passive permeability, and the closest L5 analog (M02) with the same secondary-amine plus hydroxamate motif has low Caco-2 Papp A→B (0.97×10^-6 cm/s) and a high efflux ratio (10.8), supporting gut-wall efflux and low absorption.
DMT, a tryptamine sharing the query's indole-ethylamine core, has measured absolute oral bioavailability of about 10-15% in humans, below the 20% threshold.
Sumatriptan, also a tryptamine, has consistent human oral bioavailability of 14-15% across L1 and L2 records, below the threshold.

Eluxadoline, a poorly permeable ionizable molecule, has oral bioavailability of about 1% due to low gastrointestinal permeability; the query's very low neutral fraction is an analogous permeability liability, though the query is smaller and less polar.
